THE AC OFFERED A FALLBACK ('if a branch is genuinely missing, add it') AND ADDING IT WOULD HAVE BEEN A REGRESSION. TD-073 named two opposite causes; it is (a), the gate was crying wolf, and I proved that before editing anything. ralph.sh:243 ALREADY ends the sprint from the sprint.json tally (after_complete -ge total -> 'PRD COMPLETE' -> exit 0) -- so a sprint-ending COMPLETE IS honored, via the authoritative artifact rather than the model's claim, which is STRONGER than trusting the tag. The 2026-05-12 loop-control rewrite says so in the header verbatim and even spells out 'COMPLETE when the count disagrees ... CONTINUE'. The literal drift: ralph.sh documents the tags with the ABBREVIATED `<promise>COMPLETE</>` closing form, invisible to the test's `</promise>` regex.

WHY THE BRANCH IS REFUSED, AND IT IS NOW PINNED: a tag-driven `grep COMPLETE -> exit 0` lets a model END A SPRINT BY ASSERTING COMPLETION while stories are still passes:false -- the exact failure the rewrite removed, and the worst class for this harness because it looks like it works. The ABSENCE is now a test so a future 'fix TD-073' pass cannot undo it.

BUT LOOSENING THE GATE WAS THE RUBBER STAMP THE AC FORBIDS, so I took neither branch of the false dichotomy. The old parser counted ANY full-form tag string anywhere in ralph.sh as 'handled' -- weak in BOTH directions: it misses real handling written abbreviated, and IT CAN BE SATISFIED BY A COMMENT. Net result is STRICTER: parses REAL grep branches (comments stripped FIRST, so prose mentioning a tag -- or the word 'grep' -- cannot masquerade as a branch) vs explicit `# NOT_TAG_DRIVEN: <promise>X</promise> -- <why>` declarations; no ghost branch, no ghost declaration, no tag that is BOTH.

MUTATION B IS THE LESSON AND IT IS THIS SPRINT'S LESSON A THIRD TIME (US-527 SQL-vs-pure-function, US-528 two defaulted layers, now this). I mutated the tally comparison to `if false` while LEAVING THE DECLARATION IN PLACE: THE PARITY GATE STAYED GREEN and only the mechanism test went red. A parity-only suite would ship a harness that can NEVER END A SPRINT while cheerfully documenting that it can. GENERAL RULE, NOW THRICE-PROVEN: when a contract is satisfiable by a DECLARATION, a second test must pin the MECHANISM that makes the declaration true -- asserting the declaration tests nothing. Also note test_ralphShEndsTheSprintFromTheSprintJsonTally_notFromTheTag PASSED BEFORE I touched ralph.sh: that is what converts 'the branch exists' from my claim into evidence.

Other mutations: (A) add the grep branch on COMPLETE -> 2 red; (C) bare NOT_TAG_DRIVEN with no rationale -> 1 red (the hatch cannot become a one-line silencer for any inconvenient tag); (D) DELETE the PARTIAL_BLOCKED row from prompt.md -- the direction my own US-528 note warned against, and the other way to satisfy the ORIGINAL assertion -> 2 red. All reverted + verified byte-identical against a pre-mutation snapshot (git checkout is outside the allow-list).

*** THE AC WAS WRONG AND I DID NOT IMPLEMENT IT AS WRITTEN. *** AC1 said 'pull the exact good/degraded/replace DEPTH-BAND thresholds from Spool's ruling'. No such thing exists. Spool ruled the opposite verbatim: 'Bands UNCHANGED -- good >=582 s, degraded 436-582 s, replace <436 s, on RUNTIME_BASELINE_S = 727.' Only the GATE is depth-based. Inventing per-band voltages to satisfy the AC's phrasing would have been Rule-2 fabrication AND would have traded a reachability bug for a wrong-classification bug -- worse, because it looks like it works. I implemented the ruling, flagged the wording to Marcus in completionNotes, and fixed the same bad phrase where US-526 had leaked it into architecture.md. CARRY THIS: when an AC paraphrases an SME ruling, read the ruling -- the paraphrase is what drifts.

MUTATION TESTING CAUGHT MY OWN BAD TEST, and this is the reusable lesson. The gate is enforced TWICE (read SQL + _parseRow), so the halves cover for each other. My first boundary test asserted qualifyingCount/lastHealthCheckTs and its docstring CLAIMED it proved SQL filtered shallow rows. I neutralised the SQL predicate with `AND (end_vcell_v <= ? OR 1=1)` (param count preserved so nothing errored) and ALL 44 TESTS STILL PASSED -- the pure function silently covered for it, so a real SQL regression would ship green. Rewrote to assert at the READ BOUNDARY (monkeypatch computeBatteryHealthVerdict, capture exactly which rows SQL handed over); the same mutation now fails (4 rows crossed vs 3). GENERAL RULE FOR THIS CODEBASE: when a rule is enforced in two places, a test that asserts only on the RESULT tests neither half -- assert at the seam. Note the pre-existing sibling test_readBatteryHealthVerdict_appliesTheGateInSql has the identical blind spot.

Two further mutations proving the regression cannot return: floor 60->600 = 6 red (incl. the ordering guard + both band-reachability cases); depth 3.50->3.90 = 4 red (both boundaries). All three reverted + re-verified green. The reachability guard asserts the ORDERING (QUALIFYING_MIN_RUNTIME_S < DEGRADED < GOOD) not the literal 60 -- pinning `== 60` alone would let any future floor >= 436 s silently re-break reachability.

WHAT SHIPPED: QUALIFYING_MIN_RUNTIME_S 600 -> 60 (sanity floor only) + new QUALIFYING_MAX_END_VCELL_V = 3.50, in BOTH gate halves, with end_vcell_v SELECTed and carried across the read boundary. Bands/windows/staleness/median-of-3 untouched. US-504b's prediction held exactly -- 'only the gate constant moves' -- which is why the bands were parked in a separate public verdictForMedianRuntime().
